The [[1952 Summer Olympics]], officially known as the Games of the XV Olympiad and commonly known as Helsinki 1952, were an international [[multi-sport event]] held from 19 July to 3 August 1952 in [[Helsinki]], Finland.<ref name="IOC Helsinki">{{cite web |title=Helsinki 1952 Summer Olympics – Athletes, Medal & Results |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/helsinki-1952 |website=[[International Olympic Committee]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241001123701/https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/helsinki-1952 |archive-date=2024-10-01 |url-status=live |access-date=23 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Helsinki 1952 Olympic Games |url=https://www.britannica.com/sports/Summer-Olympic-Games |website=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |date=2025-01-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126182659/https://www.britannica.com/sports/Summer-Olympic-Games |archive-date=2025-01-26 |url-status=live |last1=Johnston |first1=Mindy |access-date=24 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref> A total of 4,955 athletes representing 69 [[National Olympic Committee]]s (NOCs) participated,<ref name="IOC Helsinki" /> which included 12 teams making their Olympic China competed under the name of the [[China|People's Republic of China]] (PRC) for the first time, although they only arrived in time to participate in one event. From 1924 to 1948, athletes from [[mainland China]] competed as the delegation of the [[Republic of China at the Olympics|Republic of China]] (ROC). As a result of the [[Chinese Civil War]], a number of government and NOC representatives had fled to Taiwan and claimed to be the proper representative party of China. The [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) granted the ROC designation to the group in Taiwan and allowed both the PRC and ROC to compete with the name "China", although the latter withdrew in protest.<ref name="COC">{{cite web |title=10th-15th Olympic Games: 1936-1952 |url=http://www.china.org.cn/english/features/olympics/100673.htm |website=[[China Internet Information Center]] |date=2004-07-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421170352/http://www.china.org.cn/english/features/olympics/100673.htm |archive-date=2015-04-21 |url-status=live |access-date=27 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Chan |first=Gerald |date=Autumn 1985 |title=The "Two-Chinas" Problem and the Olympic Formula |url=https://doi.org/10.2307/2759241 |journal=[[Pacific Affairs]] |volume=58 |issue=3 |pages=473–490 |doi=10.2307/2759241 |jstor=2759241 |access-date=27 January 2025|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Medal table ==
[[File:Nina Ponomaryova 1960.jpg|thumb|alt=Nina Ponomaryova from about the highs up, posing in a way that appears to be her just finishing a discus throw. Image is in black and white.|[[Nina Ponomaryova]], pictured here at the [[1960 Summer Olympics]], was the first athlete representing the Soviet Union to win a gold medal, doing so in the [[Athletics at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Women's discus throw|women's discus throw]] event.<ref name="Soviet Gold" />]]
[[File:Asnoldo Devonish 1952 Helsinki.png|thumb|alt=Asnoldo Devonish pictured from just below the chest up and looking off to the side. Image is in black and white.|[[Asnoldo Devonish]] won Venezuela's fist Olympic medal of any kind, winning bronze in the [[Athletics at the 1952 Summer Olympics – Men's triple jump|men's triple jump]].<ref name="Venezuela IOC" />]]
The medal table is based on information provided by the IOC and is consistent with IOC conventional sorting in its published medal tables. The table uses the [[Olympic medal table]] sorting method. By default, the table is ordered by the number of gold medals the athletes from a nation have won, where a nation is an entity represented by a NOC. The number of silver medals is taken into consideration next and then the number of bronze medals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympic medal table: USA beat China to top spot at Paris 2024 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2580716.html |website=[[The Independent]] | date=11 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240812015233/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/olympics-2024-medal-table-count-paris-b2594580.html |archive-date=12 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Ostlere |first1=Lawrence |access-date=12 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=A Medal Count That Adds Up To Little |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |website=[[The New York Times]] | date=18 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230321004238/https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/19/sports/olympics/19araton.html |archive-date=21 March 2023 |url-status=live |last1=Araton |first1=Harvey |url-access=subscription |access-date=25 July 2024 }}</ref> If teams are still tied, equal ranking is given and they are listed alphabetically by their [[List of IOC country codes|IOC country code]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What happens if two countries are tied in the Olympic medal table? Tiebreaker rules explained |url=https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |website=[[Diario AS]] |date=10 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811152350/https://en.as.com/olympic_games/what-happens-if-two-countries-are-tied-in-the-olympic-medal-table-tiebreaker-rules-explained-n/ |archive-date=11 August 2024 |url-status=live |last1=Cons |first1=Roddy |access-date=11 August 2024 |language=en-us }}</ref>
